subject.title: docs: LiteLLM supply chain attack advisory (v1.82.7 / v1.82.8)

question: What exact LiteLLM install and remediation wording should OpenClaw publish in the LiteLLM provider docs for the reported compromised PyPI releases?
rationale: The docs gap is clear, but choosing third-party supply-chain remediation guidance and whether to pin fresh installs or only affected-version rollbacks needs security maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve updated advisory wording
options.body: Security maintainers choose current safe install guidance plus affected-version rollback and credential-rotation text, then a focused docs PR updates `docs/providers/litellm.md`.

options.title: Link only to upstream guidance
options.body: OpenClaw documents the incident at a high level and points users to LiteLLM/PyPI advisories for exact version guidance while still recommending credential rotation for affected proxy hosts.

options.title: Decline provider-specific advisory
options.body: Maintainers decide OpenClaw should not carry third-party LiteLLM incident guidance beyond existing provider setup docs and general security reporting paths.

recommendation.title: Approve updated advisory wording
recommendation.body: Security maintainers choose current safe install guidance plus affected-version rollback and credential-rotation text, then a focused docs PR updates `docs/providers/litellm.md`.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original LiteLLM provider work and have the strongest current-main history on the provider docs surface; security wording should still involve secops review.
